review.posthog_relevance: Modal sandbox task resource reservation and billing provisioning
review.reason: The change refactors Modal integration resource reservation to consistently return a tuple of request and limit, removing a VM-specific branch that returned a flat memory value. P1.F1.H1 demonstrates this implementation change, while P1.F2.H1 and P1.F2.H2 update corresponding test assertions. This establishes a bounded correctness improvement for the Modal managed compute provider,
review.uncertainty: No runtime or production evidence provided; benefit relies on the implementation and test assertions supplied in the patch.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains three hunks. P1.F1.H1 and P1.F2.H1 are related and demonstrate a substantive, bounded correctness improvement. P1.F2.H2 is also related and demonstrates the same improvement. No other hunks are supplied, so no unrelated PRs are flagged. No adoption, incident avoidance or effort is inferred. No tier is assigned.

observations.behavior: The implementation of resource reservation for Modal sandbox tasks was refactored. The previous implementation distinguished between VM and non-VM runtimes, returning a flat memory value for VMs while returning a tuple for non-VMs. The new implementation always returns a tuple of request and limit, removing the VM-specific branch.
observations.posthog_connection: This change affects the Modal integration, which is a managed compute provider. The change could prevent billing or provisioning errors where memory request and limit were not both supplied, potentially affecting users relying on the burstable resource configuration. This is a bounded correctness improvement.
